notes: As a regular syllable it is pronounced "ha". When used as the topic particle, は is pronounced "wa" instead.

Usually pronounced "o" when used as the object particle. The character-to-romaji mapping is kept as "wo" here to preserve the character/romaji relationship.
Katakana counterpart of the object-particle を. Rarely used outside of stylized text, since を is almost always written in hiragana.
The moraic nasal. Commonly romanized as "n"; its exact pronunciation (n/m/ng-like) shifts depending on the sound that follows it.
Katakana moraic nasal, used the same way as ん. Commonly romanized as "n"; its exact pronunciation shifts depending on the sound that follows it.
Modern pronunciation is usually identical (or very close) to じ. Kept as a separate character because it has its own spelling/usage rules (mainly in sequential voicing, e.g. はな+ぢ → はなぢ).
Katakana counterpart of ぢ. Modern pronunciation is usually identical (or very close) to ジ.

Katakana counterpart of づ. Modern pronunciation is usually identical (or very close) to ズ.
